title: README_Wound_Type_Airbrush_Dremel_2022
text:
Wound_Type_Airbrush_Dremel_2022 - README
Project Information
Title: Wound_Type_Airbrush_Dremel_2022
Principal Investigator: Adrian Stier (UCSB), Ashley Seifert (UKY), Craig Osenberg (UGA)
Collaborators: Lily Zhao, Josh Sarli, Maddie Pacheco, Molly Brzezinski
Project Dates: June 2022
Contact: Adrian Stier - astier@ucsb.edu
Research Objectives
This project investigates how corals regenerate from wounds of different severities. Specifically, we compare surface-only tissue removal via airbrush to deeper tissue and skeleton removal via Dremel rotary tool. The study aims to:
• Assess differences in regeneration between airbrush and Dremel wounds.
• Determine the time required for complete wound healing.
• Standardize imaging methods to track coral tissue recovery.
Data Sources & Collection Methods
Experimental Design
• Coral Samples: 22 samples from a previous project (March 2022, collected by Adrian, Ashley, and Lily).
• Species Representation:
  - Porites - 3 pairs
  - Acropora - 3 pairs
  - Pocillopora - 2 pairs
• Treatment Groups:
  - Group A (Airbrush) - Superficial tissue removal only.
  - Group B (Dremel) - Tissue and slight skeleton removal.
• Standardization:
  - 1 cm × 1 cm wounds created using a silicon mat stencil.
  - Josh ensured the Dremel did not bore into the skeleton where possible.
Imaging Protocol
• Baseline Photos: Immediately post-wounding.
• Subsequent Photos:
  - 72 hours post-wounding.
  - Every five days until wound regeneration was complete or until the research team left.
• Magnifications Used: Bright field images captured at 0.63× and 1.25× zoom.
• Photo Management:
  - Josh trained Maddie and Lily in microscope operation, file saving, and exporting.
  - Estimated 5–10 minutes per coral (retrieval, imaging, return).
• Photo Analysis:
  -Molly analyzed all available images for healing status as either “no”, “incomplete”, or “yes” where:
“no” indicates no qualitative change in wound healing
“incomplete” indicates that healthy tissue is progressively moving to cover the wounded tissue when compared to the previous image
“yes” indicates that the previously wounded tissue is now indecipherable from the surrounding tissue
Notes on Execution
• Project Discussion: Josh discussed methodology with Adrian and Ashley before wounding.
• Imaging Frequency: Initially planned for daily images, but adjusted to every five days for feasibility.
• Cleaning Schedule: Josh cleaned corals in the water table every 2–3 days to remove sediment.
• Photo Capture Duration: Imaging continued until Day 10, starting 1–2 days after planning discussions.
• Team Readiness: Maddie and Lily were comfortable with time commitment and execution after training.
Key Results & Current Status
• The dataset includes time-series wound recovery metrics for each coral.
• Data analysis and manuscript preparation are ongoing.
Contact for Collaboration
For access to raw data or collaboration, please contact astier@ucsb.edu.
Last Updated: 17 Apr 2025

title: README_Wound_type_2025
text:
Wound_Type_2025 - README
Project Information
Title: Wound_Type_2025
Principal Investigator: Adrian Stier (UCSB), Ashley Seifert (UKY), Craig Osenberg (UGA)
Collaborators: Molly Brzezinski (UCSB), Michelle Diminuco (UGA)
Project Dates: May - July 2025
Contact: Adrian Stier - astier@ucsb.edu
Research Objectives
This project investigates how corals (Porites and A. pulchra) regenerate from wounds of different severities. Specifically, we compare surface-only tissue removal via airbrush to deeper tissue and skeleton removal via Dremel rotary tool, and the combined effect of an airbrush-dremel wound. The study aims to:
1) Assess differences in regeneration between airbrush, Dremel, and airbrush-dremel wounds using morphological characterization from microscope imagery
Data Sources & Collection Methods
Experimental Design

• Species Representation:
  - Porites - 15 total juveniles approximately 3-5cm in height and diameter
	-5 juveniles per treatment group
  - Acropora - 15 total nubbins approximately 6cm in height
	-5 nubbins per treatment group
• Treatment Groups:
  - Airbrush - Complete tissue removal only
  - Dremel - Partial tissue removed  and skeleton damage with removal
  - Airbrush-dremel - Complete tissue removal and skeleton damage with removal
• Standardization:
  - 8 mm^2 stencil was used to standardize all three treatments

Response Variable and Methods
Response Variable
Method
Destructive?
Notes
Morphological characterization
Visual assessment (gross and microscopic)
no
Photos taken at 1.25x and 3.2x zoom

A. pulchra characteristics
- Coenosarc coverage over wound bed 
- Zooxanthellae pattern recovery including texture and coloration
- Presence of algae in the wound-bed
- Evidence of mature polyp regeneration at the center of the wound
Porites spp characteristics
- Coenosarc coverage over wound-bed (first instance and complete coverage)
- Presence of yellow aggregations
- Presence of pink hue or coloration visible in brightfield images
- Presence of rfp signal at wound edge
- Presence of gfp signal in any coral tissue
- Presence of an algal plug in the wound-bed
- Evidence of mature polyp regeneration at the center of the wound (first instance of a mature polyp and complete repopulation of polyps in the wound bed)

Imaging Protocol

• Pre-screening photos: A. pulchra and Porites spp were assessed for initial rfp, gfp autofluorescent signals
• Baseline Photos: Immediately post-wounding (D0)
• Subsequent Photos:
24 hours, 48 hours, 72 hours, 5 days, 7 days, then every seven days until wound regeneration was complete or until the research team left
• Camera specifications: 
Images captured at 1.25× and 3.2× zoom
Bright field, gfp, rfp filters used for Porites
Bright field only used for A. pulchra
• Photo Management:
Labeling scheme “species_treatment_id_day post wound_filter_zoom”
Example: “A.pulchra_Drem_109_D35_BF_3.2 zoom.tif”
Example: ”Porites_Drem_2_D35_BF_3.2 zoom.vsi”
Imaging Organization
All photos from aim 1 are located on the Stier Remote Drive accessible at smb://stier-nas1.eemb.ucsb.edu

Notes on Execution
• Project Discussion: Adrian, Ashley, Craig and Molly were involved in project planning and experimental design
• Experiment Execution:  Adrian and Craig collected and wounded corals. Ashley screened corals and performed photo-microscopy for D0-D7. Molly and Michelle maintained all aquaria and performed all photo-microscopy with characterization D7-D63. 
• Data management: Molly organized all raw data and performed QA/QC on images
• Analysis: Molly analyzed all microscope photos for characterization
• Data Analysis: Adrian performed all data analysis
• Manuscript preparation: Adrian, Ashley, Craig and Molly contributed to the final manuscript
Key Results & Current Status
• The dataset includes time-series wound recovery metrics and images for each coral for both species
Contact for Collaboration
For access to raw data or collaboration, please contact astier@ucsb.edu.

title: README_wound_type_histology_2025
text:
Wound_Type_2025 - README
Project Information
Title: Wound_Type_2025
Principal Investigator: Adrian Stier (UCSB), Ashley Seifert (UKY), Craig Osenberg (UGA)
Collaborators: Molly Brzezinski (UCSB), Michelle Diminuco (UGA)
Project Dates: June - July 2025
Contact: Adrian Stier - astier@ucsb.edu
Research Objectives
This project investigates how corals (Porites) regenerate from wounds of different severities. Specifically, we compare surface-only tissue removal via airbrush to deeper tissue and skeleton removal via Dremel rotary tool. The study aims to:
1) Assess key changes in tissue organization and cellular characteristics (migration and proliferation) using histological techniques
Data Sources & Collection Methods
Experimental Design

 • Species Representation:
Porites - 40 total fragments approximately 3-5cm in height and diameter from 10 decaying bommies (4 genetically identical corals from 10 bommies)
Each bommie was labeled with a number, and its replicate fragment was labeled with a letter such that 1A, 1B, 1C, and 1D are all fragments from bommie 1. 
• Treatment Groups:
Airbrush - Complete tissue removal only 
16 fragments from 4 bommies
Dremel - Partial tissue removed  and skeleton damage with removal
16 fragments from 4 bommies
Control - unwounded
8 fragments from 2 bommies
• Sampling timepoints:
D0 (8 control only)
D2 (4 airbrush, 4 dremel)
D7(4 airbrush, 4 dremel)
D14(4 airbrush, 4 dremel)
D21(4 airbrush, 4 dremel)
• Standardization:
  - 8 mm^2 stencil was used to standardize all three treatments
Response Variable and Methods
Response Variable
Method
Destructive?
Notes
Histological characterization
Histology
yes
TBD

Histology Protocol

Small (3-5cm diameter) porites fragments were squared off with a band-saw to isolate the ~1cm wound
Sawed fragments were gently cleaned with a plastic pasteur pipette, being careful not to disturb any algal mats
Cleaned fragments were immediately placed in 10% NBF for 16 hours, then rinsed in PBS 3x for 15 minutes, then 70% etoh  3x for 15 minutes and stored in 70% etoh from July - October (3 months)
Notes on Execution
• Project Discussion: Adrian, Ashley, Craig and Molly were involved in project planning and experimental design
• Experiment Execution: 
Histology: Molly and Ashley discussed experimental design, Molly ultimately decided sampling timepoints. Michelle and Hayden collected corals for histology. Molly screened and randomized histology corals. Michelle and Molly sampled and prepared tissue for histology
Key Results & Current Status
• Histological samples are collected, but not processed for Porites under airbrush and dremel treatments only
Contact for Collaboration
For access to raw data or collaboration, please contact astier@ucsb.edu.
